name: Lysekil
title: Lysekil Tanker Thickness Gauging | Brofjorden Crude & Products
description: Thickness gauging for crude and product tankers at Brofjorden near Lysekil: ballast tank, deck and void UTM, pre-docking steel estimates and vetting checks.
h1: Thickness Measurement for Crude and Product Tankers at Lysekil and Brofjorden
intro: Lysekil, at the mouth of the Gullmarn fjord on the Bohuslän coast, matters to tanker operators because of Brofjorden, the deep-water harbour north of the town that serves Preemraff Lysekil, Sweden's largest refinery. Crude carriers discharge at its crude jetty and product tankers lift refinery output from the product berths. Calls are short and terminal rules are strict, so gauging is planned tightly around discharge, anchorage waits and the docking ahead. Atlantis sends its technicians from India for each tanker and they join her through the ship's agent.

highlights.h: Crude carriers at a very deep jetty
highlights.p: The crude berth at Brofjorden was built for the largest crude carriers, so Aframaxes, Suezmaxes and VLCCs all discharge there. While cargo pumps run, deck structure, void spaces and segregated ballast tanks certified for entry can be gauged, always within what the terminal and master allow.

Product tankers come back to Brofjorden voyage after voyage to load refinery output. That rhythm lets an owner split a gauging programme over several calls, finishing a few ballast tanks each time, so that the full picture is ready before the ship goes to her renewal docking.

highlights.h: Waiting time at the Bohuslän anchorages
highlights.p: Tankers waiting for a berth lie at anchorage positions east of Bohus-Malmön, around Lindholmen or, for the largest ships, further offshore. A wait of a day or more, with the crew free to prepare spaces, suits deck and air-pipe gauging reached by launch.

port.h: Brofjorden and Lysekil: a refinery harbour on the Skagerrak coast
p: The Bohuslän coast is granite cut into fjords and sheltered by skerries, and Brofjorden is one of the inlets where deep water reaches close to the shore. That depth is why the refinery was sited here in the 1970s: the crude jetty near the mouth of the fjord has water enough for crude carriers of several hundred thousand tonnes deadweight, and the approach from the Skagerrak is short compared with most Baltic oil ports. Pilots from the Swedish Maritime Administration board south-west of the approach, larger ships take two pilots, and escort tugs are compulsory for laden crude tankers. Lysekil town itself lies to the south, on the peninsula at the entrance to the Gullmarn, with a harbour for small craft and a waterfront better known for summer visitors than for cargo.

Almost all the commercial shipping in the municipality belongs to the refinery. Crude arrives from the North Sea fields and from much further afield on Aframax, Suezmax and VLCC tonnage, and the refinery's petrol, diesel and other products leave on product tankers bound for Scandinavian, Baltic and wider European terminals. By tonnage handled, Brofjorden ranks among the busiest harbours in Sweden, and on most days several tankers are either alongside, approaching or at anchor. The ships are managed from all over the world, so a superintendent in Athens, Oslo or Singapore may need readings from a tanker that will spend only a day at the jetty, and Brofjorden is often the last European call before a long ballast voyage or a docking.

Weather sets the pace more than ice does. The fjord's shallow inner reaches can freeze in a hard winter, but the jetties and fairway remain in use, and the real constraint is the Skagerrak gale: in strong winds from the south-west round to the north, arrivals and departures are held and tug escorts are suspended, so a tanker may spend longer at anchor than planned. Short December daylight also limits outdoor deck work. Inspection demand reflects the trade. Tanker owners face vetting under SIRE 2.0 and charterers' age limits, so ballast tank coating condition, deck plating and the structure around manifolds and pipe supports are recurring subjects, and older ships approaching their third or fourth renewal survey often need a pre-docking steel estimate before the yard is booked.

facilities.h: Where a tanker can be gauged around Brofjorden
p: There is no drydock or tanker repair yard at Brofjorden or in Lysekil, so work here is done afloat, either alongside one of the refinery's jetties or at anchor. At the jetties the terminal's safety rules come first: equipment must be acceptable for the hazardous zones it enters, enclosed spaces are entered only on the ship's permit with a valid gas-free certificate, and the cargo operation sets the timetable. Cargo tanks stay closed during discharge or loading, so in-port scopes concentrate on segregated ballast tanks, void spaces, cofferdams, the forepeak, deck plating and longitudinals, and pipe supports on deck.

Anchorage work is reached by launch booked through the agent, and the exposed outer anchorage used by the largest crude carriers is only workable in moderate seas. For a full renewal or CAP programme, including cargo tanks, the readings taken here feed the yard where the tanker will dock. The largest crude carriers usually dock at big-ship yards far from Scandinavia, while product tankers trading in northern Europe commonly dock in Baltic, Polish or other European yards, and our team can travel there to complete the work.
list: Crude oil jetty near the fjord mouth — deck, void-space and segregated ballast tank gauging on crude carriers during discharge, within terminal and master approval.
Product jetties on the south shore of Trommekilen — ballast tank, forepeak and deck readings on product tankers while they load refinery cargo.
Anchorage positions east of Bohus-Malmön and around Lindholmen — launch-borne deck, air-pipe and accessible tank work on tankers waiting for a berth.
Deep-water anchorage south-west of the approach — waiting area for the largest crude carriers, workable for short condition checks in moderate weather.
Lysekil's town harbour — smaller craft lying in the Gullmarn gauged alongside when a job is arranged.
The tanker's docking yard — Brofjorden readings carried forward on the TM plan, or the team mobilised to the yard to finish cargo-tank gauging.

context.h: Port state control, vetting and tanker rules at Brofjorden
p: Port state control in Sweden is carried out by the Swedish Transport Agency under the Paris MoU, and oil and chemical tankers more than twelve years old fall into the Paris MoU's expanded inspection category, so the older crude carriers calling at Brofjorden can expect a thorough look at structure, ballast tanks and safety systems. Commercial scrutiny is often tougher still: oil majors and refiners screen tankers through OCIMF's SIRE 2.0 inspections and their own acceptance criteria, and a vetting observation on ballast tank coating or deck corrosion can keep a ship off charter. Ships calling at EU ports also carry an Inventory of Hazardous Materials under the EU Ship Recycling Regulation, and voyages to and from Brofjorden count towards EU ETS and FuelEU Maritime obligations.

For tankers the Enhanced Survey Programme sets the gauging pattern, with transverse sections across the cargo area and close-up survey that grows at each renewal survey, and many charterers now ask older tankers for a CAP rating as well. The corrosion that matters most on a crude carrier is often in places only reachable gas-free: bottom pitting under crude sludge, wastage under heating coils, and grooving at the bottom of longitudinals in cargo tanks. Ballast tanks, where coating breakdown starts at edges, welds and the upper parts of side tanks, are the in-port opportunity, which is why so many Brofjorden calls are used to measure them ahead of a docking.

jobs.h: Tanker gauging jobs we see at Lysekil
jobs.p: Work at Brofjorden is shaped by the refinery's cargo programme. Scopes are defined tightly in advance, agreed with the terminal through the agent, and ordered so the most important spaces are measured first in case discharge finishes early or the ship is shifted to anchor. Readings are reported to the superintendent before the tanker sails, because the next decision, whether that is a yard booking, a charter or a sale, usually cannot wait for the next call. Most requests come from superintendents preparing a docking or answering a charterer, and a few from buyers who need an independent view of a tanker that is trading and cannot be taken off hire for an inspection. Examples of jobs that fit a Brofjorden call:
list: Ballast tank and deck gauging on a Suezmax discharging crude, to firm up the steel estimate before her third renewal survey in a yard abroad.
A product tanker on regular liftings, with two or three ballast tanks gauged per call until the whole set is complete before the docking.
Deck plating, longitudinals and pipe-support structure measured on an older Aframax after a vetting observation on deck corrosion.
Pre-purchase gauging of a product tanker at anchor while she waits for a berth, scoped by the buyer's technical adviser.
Forepeak, cofferdam and void-space readings on a VLCC at the crude jetty, with cargo tanks left for the CAP survey at her next docking.

logistics: Göteborg Landvetter Airport is the nearest international gateway, and from there the team continues by road up the Bohuslän coast to Lysekil and Brofjorden. The refinery harbour is an ISPS facility with its own safety induction, so the agent registers the technicians' names and passport details with the terminal in advance and books launches for anchorage work. Sweden is a Schengen state, so the team travels from India on Schengen visas, and because tanker berthing dates move with the refinery's crude programme, we plan the visa period with room for the call to slip.

faqs.q: Can cargo tanks be gauged while a tanker is alongside at Brofjorden?
faqs.a: Not during cargo operations. Entering a cargo tank needs it to be cleaned, ventilated and certified gas-free, which does not happen while crude is being discharged or products loaded. What can be done alongside is ballast tank, void space, cofferdam, forepeak and deck gauging, provided the master and the terminal agree. Cargo-tank readings for a renewal survey or CAP belong at the docking yard.

faqs.q: Is gauging at the Lysekil anchorages realistic?
faqs.a: Yes, when the sea state allows a safe launch transfer. The anchorage positions closer to the coast are more sheltered than the deep-water area used by the largest crude carriers. A tanker waiting a day or two can have deck plating, air pipes and prepared ballast tanks measured, and we arrange the scope so that the priority readings are taken first in case the ship is called to the jetty.

faqs.q: Where do tankers from Brofjorden go for dry-docking?
faqs.a: There is no tanker drydock in Lysekil. VLCCs and Suezmaxes usually dock at large yards outside Scandinavia, while product tankers in northern European trade often use Baltic or Polish yards. Readings taken at Brofjorden are recorded against the TM plan's frames and sections, so the yard and the class surveyor can plan steel and close-up survey from them, and our team can follow the tanker to complete the programme.

faqs.q: How does winter weather on the Skagerrak affect a job?
faqs.a: Gales are the main risk. In strong winds from the westerly sectors, tanker movements and escort-tug operations at Brofjorden are suspended, so a ship can spend extra time at anchor or alongside. Short daylight in midwinter limits deck work, though work inside ballast tanks is not affected. We keep the team's dates flexible and stay in contact with the agent on the berthing schedule.
